title: Offline-first bootstrap & deterministic artifact replication acceptance criteria for VPC/private deployments
creator: Priya Desai
description: Define concrete requirements and testable acceptance criteria for an "offline-first" bootstrap and deterministic artifact replication strategy for Private/VPC deployments. Target outcome: customers operating in isolated or restricted egress environments can reliably install, upgrade, and validate Redwood Private with zero external write dependencies and cryptographic artifact verification.
background: Customers deploying Redwood Private in high-security environments require a reliable offline install and upgrade flow. Existing acceptance criteria focus on network compatibility and basic offline bundle syncs, but we lack a deterministic artifact replication contract and staged promotion for mirrors. This ticket consolidates requirements across networking, artifact provenance, signing, and upgrade choreography so engineering and support have a single source of truth for ship criteria.
scope: Acceptance criteria and test plans for: 1) deterministic artifact replication and manifest pinning for images and tarballs, 2) offline bootstrap with optional signed media (physical or repo mirror), 3) staged mirror promotion and rollback choreography for upgrades, 4) validation hooks for KMS/HSM key rotation in air-gapped environments. Includes operator-facing docs required for customer handoff.
non_goals: Implementing a GUI for mirror management (docs + CLI only)
Building an official physical media distribution service (we will document supported third-party processes)
Changing underlying image signing scheme (we will define compatibility requirements; cryptographic work occurs in a follow-up ticket)
acceptance_criteria: AC-1: Offline bootstrap succeeds from a local mirror when cluster nodes have zero outbound write access and only limited inbound TLS access to designated mirror IPs. Installation completes end-to-end and API healthcheck returns 200 within configured health timeout.

AC-2: All runtime artifacts (container images, Helm charts, tarballs, and runtime configuration manifests) are referenced by manifest files containing SHA256 digests. Installer refuses to use artifacts that do not match digest pinning.

AC-3: Artifact manifests are cryptographically signed. Installer verifies signature against a root public key provided during bootstrap; verification failure aborts install with actionable error and exit codes.

AC-4: Mirror promotion flow: operators can stage a mirror with a 'staged' flag and then atomically promote to 'primary' without requiring full cluster restart. Promotion completes with <5% request error increase and zero sustained 5xx spike after promotion (measured over 10 minutes).

AC-5: Upgrade can be performed from mirror-only artifacts with an automated preflight that validates digests, signatures, available disk space, and node compatibility. Preflight produces a machine-readable report and a UI/CLI summary.

AC-6: Rollback plan executes deterministically: when an upgrade is rolled back, cluster returns to prior artifact digests and configurations, and KV-cache and ephemeral state are reconciled to avoid divergence. Test harness validates 95% parity in request traces pre/post rollback for synthetic traffic.

AC-7: KMS/HSM rotation: in offline mode we support a key rotation handshake that relies only on signed rotation manifests delivered via mirror. Rotation steps and failure modes are documented; successful rotations must leave no orphaned keys referenced by live configs.

AC-8: Network port & proxy contract is documented and validated: the installer requires only outbound TCP/443 to configured mirror endpoints and optional TCP/5222 for console agent; explicit firewall rules are provided and unit tests simulate blocked ports to verify clear failure messages.

AC-9: Validation harness: an automated test suite executes in customer-like VPC (simulated air-gapped) and reports pass/fail for each AC with logs collected and uploadable via customer-approved methods (s3-gateway or physical media).
rollout_plan: Phase 1: API/CLI spec and test harness (week 1-3) - implement digest checks, signature verification, and manifest format. Deliver: spec + reference CLI.
Phase 2: Mirror promotion & upgrade choreography (week 4-6) - implement staged promotion flags and preflight checks. Deliver: CLI workflows + runbook.
Phase 3: KMS rotation offline contract & docs (week 7-8) - deliver rotation manifests, docs, and sample scripts for customers.
Phase 4: Customer beta + verification (week 9-12) - onboard 2 pilot customers in isolated VPCs, gather telemetry and update docs.
GA: public docs, runbooks, and integration tests published alongside release private-2026.04
test_plan: TP-1: Simulated air-gap e2e: provision test VPC with no external egress except mirror IPs; run full install and upgrade from mirror; collect logs and metrics.
TP-2: Manifest tamper test: change artifact digest in mirror after initial sync and ensure installer detects mismatch and rejects artifact.
TP-3: Signature failure test: use invalid signing key and ensure failure modes provide remediation steps and non-ambiguous diagnostic codes.
TP-4: Promotion stress test: perform mirror promote while synthetic traffic is 90th percentile; measure error rates, request latency, and recovery time.
TP-5: Rollback fidelity test: upgrade, introduce a controlled fault, and perform rollback; verify service-level parity and data consistency.
TP-6: KMS offline rotation simulation: run rotation manifests from mirror and verify no secret leakage and clean key state.
TP-7: Firewall/Proxy blocking test: intentionally block required ports and verify installer surfaces clear advice and fails safely.
TP-8: Documentation usability check: provide runbook to a support engineer unfamiliar with the system and time them through an offline bootstrap; record completion time and confusion points.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Customers maintain mirrors incorrectly causing stale artifacts. Mitigation: provide an automated reconciliation tool and TTL-based alerts; include explicit mirror health checks in the preflight.

Risk: Signature key compromise or mismatch. Mitigation: require signed rotation manifests and provide a clear emergency key-revocation flow in docs; mandate offline key custody guidance for customers.
Risk: Complex rollback edge-cases for stateful components. Mitigation: define strict pre-upgrade snapshot requirements and automated validation that snapshots are restorable before proceeding.

Risk: Customers expect physical media distribution. Mitigation: document recommended third-party services and provide a checklist for secure media ingestion but mark physical distribution as out-of-scope for this ship.
Risk: Inconsistent proxy behavior across customer environments. Mitigation: publish a minimal proxy test harness and explicit connectivity diagnostics with remediation steps.
notes: Design review required for manifest format: involve SecOps and Applied ML infra teams.
Coordinate with Console team to ensure preflight reports can be uploaded to customer telemetry endpoints when allowed.
Align with legal/compliance on guidance for key custody and physical media handling prior to GA.
